inline_comments.comment: The semver level is `patch`, but `patch` is reserved for bug fixes. Adding a new community integration entry to the docs is a net-new additive change, which requires `minor`. Per the project rules: "Do not accept `patch` for a net-new feature."
Typo: "marmaid.js" should be "mermaid.js". This same misspelling appears in all three changeset files.
The semver level is `major`, which is only appropriate for breaking changes. Adding documentation for a new community integration is additive and non-breaking; it should be `minor`.

This file is an exact duplicate of `.changeset/full-clubs-learn.md` — same semver level (`major`), same message. One of the two must be deleted. Additionally, `major` is the wrong semver level here; it should be `minor` for an additive documentation change.

The `docs/` directory is auto-generated from `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` by the docs-build pipeline. Generated files carry a header warning against direct edits. All documentation changes must be made exclusively in the source tree (`packages/mermaid/src/docs/`); the generated `docs/` output must not be edited directly in a PR.

The top-level link target `https://octave.org/` is the generic GNU Octave homepage, not a Mermaid-specific page. Project rules require that new community-integration entries link directly to the integration's Mermaid- or diagram-specific documentation page, not just the product's root homepage (similar to how the Obsidian and Observable entries link directly to Mermaid-relevant pages). The top-level link should point to `https://gnu-octave.github.io/packages/octave_mermaid_js/` or the GitHub repo for `octave_mermaid_js` instead.

The sub-items "News" (a plain text changelog file), "Source Code" (the repo root), and "Bug Tracker" (GitHub Issues) are development/maintenance links, not integration resources for users. Looking at all other entries in this file, sub-items represent distinct integrations or user-facing features (e.g., GitHub sub-items are each a separate plugin or workflow tool). A single package's changelog, source repo, and issue tracker do not belong as parallel list entries in a community integrations list — they are the kind of links that appear in a README. Consider replacing all five sub-items with a single well-chosen link (e.g., the Function Reference or the Octave Repo Index) that helps users understand and adopt the integration.

The ✅ checkmark on "News", "Source Code", and "Bug Tracker" is semantically incorrect. Per the project convention, ✅ means "native Mermaid support on that platform." A GitHub NEWS file, the source repository root, and a GitHub Issues tracker are not platforms with native Mermaid support — the checkmark should be removed from these sub-items.

general_comments.comment: Three changeset files were submitted (`7123.md`, `full-clubs-learn.md`, `true-parrots-build.md`) for a single logical change. Only one changeset file is needed. Two of the three (`full-clubs-learn.md` and `true-parrots-build.md`) are byte-for-byte identical, indicating an accidental duplicate. The surviving changeset should use `minor` semver (additive feature, not a breaking change or bug fix) and fix the "marmaid" → "mermaid" typo in the message.

The PR title and all three changeset message bodies contain the same typo: "marmaid.js" instead of "mermaid.js". While the changeset message is not user-visible in the UI, it does appear in the generated CHANGELOG.md and should be spelled correctly.
